questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 22 m/s over 6 s. Its average acceleration is closest to:
questions.explanation: Average acceleration a = (vf - vi)/t = (22 - 10)/6 = 12/6 = 2 m/s^2.

questions.question: A 5 kg box is pushed with 30 N across a floor. If friction is 10 N opposite motion, the net force is:
questions.explanation: Net force equals applied minus friction: 30 N - 10 N = 20 N forward.

questions.question: A runner covers 400 m in 50 s at nearly constant speed. Average speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed v = d/t = 400/50 = 8 m/s.

questions.question: An object in uniform circular motion at speed v around radius r has centripetal acceleration:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is a_c = v^2 / r toward the center.
steps: Square speed and divide by radius
questions.fastStrategy: Circle accel rule: v-squared over r.

questions.question: A 2 kg cart moving at 3 m/s sticks to a 4 kg cart at rest. Combined speed right after collision is:
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: initial p = 2×3 = 6 kg·m/s. Total mass = 6 kg, so v = 6/6 = 1 m/s.

questions.question: Work done by a 50 N force moving an object 3 m in the force direction is:
questions.explanation: Aligned work W = F d = 50×3 = 150 J.

questions.question: A 1,000 kg car brakes from 20 m/s to rest. The change in kinetic energy is:
questions.fastStrategy: Half m v^2 → 500×400 = 200k; braking makes it negative.

questions.question: A 10 kg crate on a horizontal floor has μ_k = 0.3. The friction force while sliding is closest to:
A ball is thrown straight up at 14 m/s. Ignoring air, time to reach the top is about:
questions.explanation: Use v = v0 - g t. Set v = 0: t = v0/g ≈ 14/9.8 ≈ 1.4 s.

questions.question: A jogger runs 3 km east then 4 km west. The displacement magnitude is:
questions.explanation: Net displacement = 4 west - 3 east = 1 km west; magnitude 1 km.

questions.question: According to Newton's third law, when you push a wall with 100 N, the wall:

choices.D: Pushes you only if it moves

questions.explanation: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction; the wall pushes back with 100 N.
questions.fastStrategy: Third law = equal magnitude, opposite direction.

questions.question: A worker lifts a 20 kg box straight up 1.5 m in 2 s. Average power output is about:
questions.explanation: Work = m g h ≈ 20×9.8×1.5 ≈ 294 J. Power = 294/2 ≈ 147 W, closest to 150 W.

questions.question: A 0.5 kg ball experiences an impulse of 3 N·s. The change in velocity magnitude is:
questions.explanation: Impulse J = m Δv ⇒ Δv = J/m = 3 / 0.5 = 6 m/s.

questions.question: A crate slides down a 30° frictionless incline from rest. Its acceleration along the plane is:
questions.explanation: For a frictionless incline, a = g sinθ. With θ = 30°, sin 30° = 0.5 → a ≈ 9.8×0.5 = 4.9 m/s^2.
questions.fastStrategy: At 30°, acceleration is half of g.

questions.question: Two forces act on a mass: 12 N right and 5 N left. The net acceleration of a 3 kg mass is:
questions.explanation: Net force = 12 - 5 = 7 N right. a = F/m = 7/3 ≈ 2.3 m/s^2 right.

questions.question: A 15 N horizontal pull moves a sled 6 m in 4 s at constant speed. The opposing friction force is:
questions.explanation: Constant speed → net force zero, so friction balances the 15 N pull.

questions.question: A 0.2 kg stone is whirled horizontally on a string at 10 m/s in a 0.5 m radius circle. The required tension is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force F = m v^2 / r = 0.2×100/0.5 = 20/0.5 = 40 N.

questions.question: A block lifted slowly at constant speed with 120 N of force through 0.8 m gains gravitational potential energy of:
questions.explanation: At constant speed, lift force equals weight (120 N). Work = F d = 120×0.8 = 96 J, which equals the PE gained.

questions.question: A 50 kg passenger experiences an upward elevator acceleration of 1.5 m/s^2. The normal force from the floor is closest to:
A 0.25 kg puck moving at 8 m/s rebounds straight back at 6 m/s after hitting a wall. The momentum change magnitude is:
A 600 W motor lifts a 120 N load straight up at constant speed. The maximum speed it can sustain is about:
questions.explanation: For constant speed, P = F v → v = P/F = 600/120 = 5 m/s.

questions.question: A 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s has the same kinetic energy as a 6 kg object moving at approximately:
steps: Compute KE of first object (24 J)

questions.question: A force does negative work on an object. Its kinetic energy will:
questions.explanation: By the work-energy theorem, negative work removes energy, reducing kinetic energy.

questions.question: A 10 kg cart moves at 6 m/s. A constant 5 N opposite force acts for 4 s. The change in speed is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = F/m = -5/10 = -0.5 m/s^2. Over 4 s, Δv = -0.5×4 = -2 m/s.
questions.fastStrategy: Half m/s^2 for 4 s → subtract 2 m/s.

questions.question: Two equal masses move toward each other at equal speeds and stick together. Their final velocity is:
questions.explanation: Momenta are equal and opposite, so total momentum is zero. After sticking, the combined mass must have zero velocity.
steps: Note equal masses and opposite velocities
